title: Pahlavi Dynasty
capsule: The Pahlavi dynasty ruled Iran from 1925 to 1979 through two monarchs: Reza Shah Pahlavi (r. 1925–1941), who abolished the Qajar dynasty, centralized power, and pursued forced modernization and secularization modeled on Atatürk's Turkey; and his son Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi (r. 1941–1979). The latter era included the CIA- and MI6-backed coup of 1953 (Operation AJAX/Boot) that restored the Shah after the nationalization crisis under Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh, followed by the White Revolution reforms of 1963. Despite oil wealth and rapid industrialization, the Shah's autocratic rule and the SAVAK secret police generated broad opposition; the Islamic Revolution of 1978–79, led by Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, forced the Shah into exile on 16 January 1979, ending the dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Iran's borders under the Pahlavis are precisely attested through modern cartography and treaties; the dynasty's territorial footprint is essentially identical to present-day Iran.
